answer: A practical defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to lock a small, time-frozen stake and build a record of useful work before it can earn trust. Like water carving a canyon, reputation should accumulate slowly through repeated, checkable actions, while a glacier of locked stake makes mass-created identities costly to abandon. Trust can also spread like a vine, through introductions from already-trusted agents, so a lone sybil with no connections stays isolated even if it passes a single check.
